excerpt: Create your first agent with a single command and start building.
Add a tool to an agent by importing the tool and passing it to the agent constructor as a tools object.
Studio is the interface for building, testing, and managing agents, workflows, and tools.
Add Mastra to an existing project, or create a new app with your preferred framework:
Browse [templates](https://mastra.ai/templates) for complete Mastra projects you can clone and adapt.
Self-hosting removes the third party, preventing sensitive data from reaching models outside of your network.
To hide external providers from Studio's model picker, set `AUTO_BLOCK_EXTERNAL_PROVIDERS=true` in your `.env` so users can only select models from your own gateways.
Compose typed steps, retries, and branches into production workflows your team can inspect and ship.
Give agents durable context with observational memory, semantic recall, and thread-aware storage.
Coordinate multi-mode agents with shared state, threads, and storage — the same harness that runs Mastra Code.
Register agents and workflows on one Mastra server, run it locally, and deploy the same app to Mastra Cloud.
Score agent runs against repeatable checks before changes reach production.
Track latency, cost, model calls, and tool usage across every production agent run.
Capture traces and user feedback into versioned datasets for repeatable evaluation.
Inspect every model call, tool call, and handoff from one searchable timeline.
Subscribe agent threads to external resources and route webhook or polling events into notification signals.
Mastra's model routing connects to 90+ providers through one standard interface.
Mastra workflows also support human-in-the-loop functionality, allowing developers to suspend a workflow and await user input or approval before resuming.
Mastra supports authoring Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, exposing agents, tools and other structured resources via the MCP interface.
Mastra includes optional built-in deployers for Vercel, Netlify and Cloudflare to automate the deployment process.
Mastra also provides guardrails to process inputs and outputs, helping prevent prompt injection and sanitize responses.
Mastra bundles agents and workflows directly into existing React, Next.js and Node.js apps, or ships them as standalone endpoints.
A user said they had many problems with LangChain and are very happy since switching to Mastra.

A commenter objected to the 'open-source' label: Mastra uses the Elastic v2 license, which says 'You may not provide the software to third parties as a hosted or managed service,' so they argue it isn't actually open source.

A self-described happy Mastra user said it strikes the right balance between higher-level abstractions and lower-level controls when needed. They looked at a handful of other frameworks first, and Mastra's clarity and ease of use stood out.
A user said they learned everything about how agents work by using Mastra's framework and going through its documentation, and that the founders are very hands-on and helpful.
A user said Mastra has an interesting set of abstractions that address many pain points of building agents, and that the team is eager to help.

A commenter criticized the landing-page workflow example (.step().then().after().then().commit()) as a very awkward way to represent the pictured graph, noting it is only a simple static workflow, not an agent.

A skeptic said there are hundreds of similar frameworks because orchestrating tools with a model is the easy part, about 5% of the work. In their view, these frameworks focus on the trivial and leave developers to handle the other 95%.
A user said they have been using Mastra for side projects for months and find it phenomenal.

A user who has been building with Mastra for a couple of weeks said they love it. They called building on top of the Vercel AI SDK a good decision, with the AI SDK as the low-level library and Mastra as the framework.

After three months with Mastra, a user called it awesome and best in class for TypeScript. However, workflows and branching logic with non-LLM, rules-based steps felt clunky. After a couple of weeks of frustration, they switched to their own custom branching workflows.
A user ran through the quickstart, created a first agent, chatted with it, and praised the nice UI and systems, though they weren't yet sure what to build.

A user said Mastra is batteries-included and opinionated, so it is hard to stay productive when you don't fit an existing pattern. Their team repeatedly had to create its own Hono routes and is now rebuilding everything with LangGraph/LangChain, while still crediting Mastra's TypeScript-first approach and good ideas.
A user complained that the pricing page doesn't seem to show any prices.
A commenter pointed to the Brex CTO describing Mastra as part of Brex's AI engineering stack as an independent third-party endorsement.
Report cited by StepSecurity's Threat Intelligence Team: multiple Mastra npm packages were identified as compromised.
